I have completed the repository database scalability analysis and submitted the structured report. Summary (high level):

- Top concern: Non-atomic checkout/coupon flow in src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (coupon decrement + order updates not wrapped in one transaction). This is a critical correctness risk under concurrent checkouts.
- Other important issues:
  - No centralized cache for hot read endpoints (product pages, cart) — will overload DB at 100k+ users.
  - N+1 / repeated DB roundtrips detected in webhook and UI flows (webhooks, CartProvider, ProductPage).
  - Schema has few explicit indexes; add indexes on hot FK columns (e.g., Review.productId, WishlistItem.userId/productId).
  - Connection pooling: Prisma global singleton is used and prisma-accelerate detected — good; ensure pooler is correctly configured.

Tools used: getDependencies, get_graph_stats, list_flows, get_flow, getCodeBlock, getRepoTree, searchCode, getSchemaDefinitions, checkConnectionPool.

Confidence: 0.78. If you'd like, I can:
- Draft exact Prisma transaction code snippets to fix checkout and cart item flows.
- Prepare SQL for adding recommended indexes.
- Propose a caching plan (what to cache, TTLs, where: Redis/edge).

No caching for hot read endpoints (product pages, cart) — sustained DB read load will saturate

findings.title: Checkout flow (order create/update) and coupon decrement are not executed atomically
findings.detail: The checkout handler performs a coupon lookup and decrement (prisma.coupon.findUnique + prisma.coupon.update) and later executes multiple order-related writes (existing order update, per-item update/create/delete, or order.create). Those steps are separate awaited Prisma calls and are not wrapped in a single transaction. Under concurrent checkouts this can cause double-consumption of coupon quantities and partially-updated orders.
findings.breaksAt: Concurrent checkout/coupon redemptions — risk appears at moderate concurrency and will reliably fail under high concurrency (10k+ concurrent checkout attempts or bursts).
findings.fix: Wrap coupon decrement + order lookup/create/update + all orderItem upserts/deletes inside a single Prisma transaction (prisma.$transaction(async (tx)=>{...})) or use DB row-level locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) or optimistic locking on coupons to reserve usage atomically.

locations: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts lines ~101-190 (existingOrder updates and per-item prisma calls)

findings.title: No centralized cache for hot read endpoints (products and cart)
findings.detail: Product endpoint returns the full product payload including related collections on every request and cart GET fetches product metadata for all items in the cart. The repository has no caching SDK (e.g., Redis). These un-cached read-heavy endpoints will generate sustained load on the database under traffic.
findings.breaksAt: Sustained high read traffic (100k+ users or many concurrent product/cart requests) — DB CPU/IOPS and latency will degrade and become the bottleneck.
findings.fix: Introduce a caching layer (Redis, Memcached, or edge/CDN/ISR). Cache product payloads and computed aggregates (review count/average). For cart reads, cache product metadata and use short-lived per-user caches or invalidate on mutations.

locations: src/app/api/products/[slug]/route.ts lines 11-29 (includes reviews, colors, videos, dummyImages in a single response)
src/app/api/cart/route.ts lines 65-77 (prisma.product.findMany for productIds in cart)
getDependencies output: no Redis or caching SDK detected

findings.title: Repeated DB roundtrips and N+1 risk in webhook and UI flows
findings.detail: Graph flagged N+1 risk for multiple flows. Example: webhooks handler uses prisma.user.findUnique then conditionally prisma.user.update or prisma.user.create (two roundtrips) instead of an upsert. CartProvider and ProductPage flows were flagged as db-heavy/N+1. Extra roundtrips amplify load during spikes (webhook bursts, many cart refreshes).
findings.breaksAt: High webhook/event volume or many concurrent client cart refreshes (tens of thousands of requests) — extra roundtrips amplify DB load and latency.
findings.fix: Replace findUnique + conditional create/update with prisma.upsert where appropriate, batch queries where possible, or wrap in transactions. Avoid fetching full related collections when only counts/aggregates are needed.

locations: src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts lines 133-165 (findUnique then update/create in handleUserCreated)
list_flows: POST /api/webhooks/clerk has dbCallCount=5 and hasN1Risk=true; CartProvider and ProductPage flagged hasN1Risk=true

findings.title: Missing explicit indexes on hot foreign-key lookup columns
findings.detail: Schema extraction shows only 4 explicit indexes across the schema. Several FK columns used in WHERE clauses are not explicitly indexed (e.g., Review.productId, Review.userId, WishlistItem.userId/productId) which will cause slow scans on large tables and degrade join/filter performance.
findings.breaksAt: Large tables (100k+ rows) — joins and WHERE filters on unindexed columns will cause high latency and DB CPU usage.
findings.fix: Add targeted indexes such as @@index([productId]) on Review, @@index([userId]) on Review and WishlistItem, and indexes on other frequently filtered FK columns. Validate improvements via EXPLAIN on heavy queries.

locations: prisma/schema.prisma Review model (~lines 141-162) — no @@index on productId/userId
prisma/schema.prisma WishlistItem model (~lines 179-193) — only @@unique([userId, productId]) and no separate indexes for common lookups

findings.title: Serverless Next.js uses Prisma singleton and Prisma Accelerate detected
findings.detail: src/lib/prisma.ts implements a global singleton PrismaClient (recommended for Next.js serverless). checkConnectionPool detected prisma-accelerate as an external pooler; this mitigates serverless connection storms if configured correctly.
findings.breaksAt: If the external pooler (prisma-accelerate) is removed or misconfigured, serverless deployments could exhaust DB connections under spikes.
findings.fix: Keep the global singleton pattern. Ensure prisma-accelerate (or another pooler) is correctly configured and documented. If removing the pooler, provide an alternative pool solution or set explicit connection limits.
